svg.text: PDF and YouTube Ingestion Architecture
Two separate input paths that join one common backend pipeline, from upload to searchable, citable chunks

g.text: • Synchronous call: the backend answers only after indexing and activation.
• Re-ingestion is safe: a failed attempt keeps the previous generation active.
• The backend fetches files only from INGEST_ALLOWED_ORIGINS and never logs the URL.
• No OCR for scanned pages · MP4 rejected · videos need captions.

Technical notes
• Ingestion is synchronous: POST /v1/ingest returns 200 only after the chunks are indexed and the new
generation is activated. The upload request waits up to 5 minutes.
• Generations: each ingestion gets a new generation number. A failed attempt leaves the previous generation
active; partial chunks are never searchable.
• Chunk limits: at most 1,200 characters, and the embedding text must fit a 512-token budget counted as bytes
(about 496 bytes). The byte budget is usually the tighter limit.
• Pages without a text layer (scanned PDFs) produce no text; OCR is not on this path. MP4 uploads are
rejected. YouTube videos without captions cannot be ingested.
• A processing lease (renewed every 30 s, expires after 6 min) lets the app recover files left in 'processing'
after a crash.
EduCopilot — Multi-Modal Educational Intelligence Copilot · Accion Labs industry project (2026) · verified final integrated build, local demo configuration (not a production deployment)
